lines.vo: Around 1939, RCA made a film to introduce something new to America: television.
"After ten years of experiment," it says, television was "first shown to the public at the World's Fair."
The set? "Much like a radio in appearance," with a screen and a "slanted mirror that reflects the image."
In the camera, the iconoscope "turns the image into electricity." In the receiver, the kinescope "recreates the image."
The signal went out from a transmitter "atop the Empire State Building."
But the limit was the horizon: "only as far as the eye can see on a perfectly clear day."
A typical program? A horse race, with a camera "atop the grandstand."
"And so," the film says, "a new American industry has been born."
In 1950, the census found that twelve percent of U.S. homes had a TV.
By January 1958, eighty-three percent of U.S. households had a TV, according to the Census Bureau.
Would you have bought a TV in 1939? Yes or no?
